source_defaults.notes: Candidate-authored platform text or direct candidate response. The original source's words and timing are retained. Claims about accomplishments, finances, opponents and policy effects are attributed rather than independently verified.

sources.speaker: Shaun Laden
sources.notes: Direct candidate statement in Sahan Journal. The original May27 publication and September5 modification are verified from the same webpage's JSON-LD, so the retained current body remains timing-qualified. An old HTTP canonical metadata URL is matched to the same HTTPS hostname/path; no source identity is changed. Allegations concerning the other candidate are not used as policy evidence.

statements.quote: grants going towards community built homes, not corporate developers
statements.claim: Proposes grants for community-built housing and zoning changes for additional dwelling units.

statements.quote: Passing a robust Capitol Investment bill (bonding)
statements.claim: Prioritizes a bonding package covering housing alongside water, transit, roads and parks.

statements.quote: strengthen tenant protections and build more public housing
statements.claim: Calls for more housing, public housing and tenant protections rather than relying on production alone.
Names universal healthcare as a top priority and later in the answer supports the Healthcare for All bill.

statements.quote: everyone has access to quality, accessible, low cost healthcare
statements.claim: States universal healthcare access as a goal and describes participation in the Minnesota Health Plan Caucus. This is not proof of an identical financing design to Freeberg's proposal.

statements.quote: expanding rights for workers to organize a union
statements.claim: Supports expanding union-organizing rights to increase workers' power.

statements.quote: All workers have a right to collectively bargain
statements.claim: Supports collective bargaining rights, living wages, paid leave, pensions and safe workplaces.
Supports wider unionization rights, prevailing wages and unionized public contracting.

statements.quote: The surplus should first be used to fully fund our schools.
statements.claim: Prioritizes school funding and community housing grants, arguing that underfunded institutions mean the surplus is not truly spare money.

statements.quote: I supported the compromise deal with the Republicans
statements.claim: Supports a negotiated package of tax relief, renter/childcare credits, school and care-worker funding, local aid and capital investment. The full multi-paragraph answer is not reduced to tax cuts alone.
Presents union leadership and everyday material security as more important than placement on an ideological spectrum. He does not say he rejects all compromise.
Calls herself a pragmatic progressive and says compromise may yield partial progress.

statements.quote: building more housing won’t be enough on its own
statements.claim: Supports additional housing while emphasizing protection against displacement; the source does not support a simple anti-building label.
Opposes Line3 and permitting the named PolyMet and Twin Metals mines, alongside a union-centered clean-energy transition.

statements.quote: a robust labor movement is central to achieving progressive change
statements.claim: Presents organized labor as central to progressive change and lists wage, leave and workplace protections.

statements.quote: bring my experience in creating progressive change
statements.claim: Presents leadership of the educators' strike and wage gains as preparation to deliver progressive change in the Senate. His claimed record is attributed, not independently audited.
Supports a statewide $15 minimum wage rising with living costs.

statements.quote: I support the right to strike and oppose the replacement of striking workers.
statements.claim: Explicitly supports strike rights and opposes replacing striking workers.

comparisons.analysis: Freeberg specifies community-housing grants and zoning changes; Pappas prioritizes a broader capital-bonding package that includes housing. Both support public investment rather than expressing opposing housing goals.

Freeberg foregrounds community-built housing grants; Ellis foregrounds additional public housing and tenant protections. These approaches are compatible, and Ellis's questionnaire nonresponse does not mean she lacked a housing platform.
Both state a goal of healthcare access for everyone. Their selected answers do not establish identical financing, benefits or implementation.
Both support workers' organizing and collective-bargaining rights.
Both support expanding union-organizing rights. A DSA endorsement is not the exclusive basis for support of this proposal.

Freeberg prioritizes underfunded schools and community housing; Pappas describes a compromise combining tax relief and public spending. The full Pappas answer contains substantial public investment and is not coded as a cuts-only agenda.

Freeberg frames politics around union leadership and people before profit; Pappas foregrounds pragmatic compromise toward progressive goals. Freeberg's answer does not establish categorical opposition to compromise.

Both present organized labor as a route to progressive change. This is shared campaign framing, not proof of identical policy platforms; Laden's retained article carries a post-primary revision qualification.

source_attempts.notes: The publisher lists no response from Ellis for each question in this series. Her archived Senate campaign platform independently supplies her actual positions; another candidate's response is not attributed to her.
